text:
[LDET.5.9] **The order is a function of the activation set, never of how the
set was reached.** [LDET.5.4] and [LDET.5.5] order the activations that are
eligible in this cycle. Whether an activation became eligible because a fact
was asserted, or because a negated condition stopped being satisfied and
released it, **must not** affect where it fires.

Concretely: **blocking does not unassign a creation timetag, and unblocking
does not mint one.** [LDET.5.5]'s timetag is assigned when the partial match
completes; a match that completed and was then held back by a negated
condition has already completed. When it is released it fires in the position
its original timetag gives it. Two engines that agree on working memory and on
the match set therefore agree on the order, whatever bookkeeping either uses to
track blocked tokens.

**This is forced by [LDET.1.1], not chosen.** The guarantee is over the fact
stream: the same rules and the same stream replay bit-for-bit. A replay
reconstructs working memory **by assertion** — it has no blocker to retract,
because the recording carries facts and not the network's internal history — so
an order that depended on the traversal that released blocked tokens would
differ between a run and its own replay, in the same runtime, on the same
machine. A determinism guarantee that fails on replay is not one. So
restoration order cannot be observable, and this clause says so rather than
leaving it to be re-derived.

**What it costs, stated plainly.** [IRET.7] calls a NOT node's bookkeeping an
implementation detail, and it is one only while its traversal order is
unobservable. An engine that fires released activations in the order its
blocked-token structure happens to yield does not conform.

**What this does not settle** ([STYL.2.15.4]). It does not say how an engine
represents a held-back match, nor that it must retain one at all: an engine
free to recompute the match on release conforms, provided the timetag it fires
under is the one the match first completed with. What is fixed is the
observable, and the observable is that the order carries no information about
the blocking.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__refresh_settled
idris.note: Refreshing a settled token is the identity.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__refresh_with_settled
idris.note: Refreshing with the blocking it already has is the identity.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__refresh_tok
idris.note: Recompute a token's blocking against the live `no` facts.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__refresh_with
idris.note: Blocking never moves a token and release never mints a new one: the same entry stays at the same position and only `blocked` (and, on release, `fired`) changes -- the clause's "blocking does not unassign a creation timetag, and unblocking does not mint one".

idris.name: iret_19_2__retract
idris.note: The retract dispatch stamps what it releases against the working memory the retraction found: a match a NOT node releases takes the timetag it first completed with, and the survivors' relative order is the same under either working memory (`ldet_5_9__before_remove`). The stamp is history-free by construction, and `iret_19_2__retract_ordered` proves the terminal stays sorted.

idris.name: ldet_5_5__before
idris.note: A function of the two matches and of working memory alone, never of how either was reached: a released match is inserted at the place its key gives it, which is the clause's 'the position its original timetag gives it'. That every agenda is sorted by it after any history is `ldet_5_9__order_after_history`.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__before_keys_shift
idris.note: The renumbering preserves the key order between any two surviving keys, empty or not.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__before_remove
idris.note: THE ORDER BETWEEN TWO SURVIVING MATCHES IS THE SAME UNDER THE WORKING MEMORY BEFORE AND AFTER A RETRACTION: what lets the retract dispatch stamp a released match against the working memory it found, which is the match's original timetag.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__before_shift
idris.note: The renumbering preserves the key order between two surviving non-empty keys.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__key_neq
idris.note: No position of a surviving match's key is the removed position.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__key_remove
idris.note: A surviving match's key after a retraction is its renumbered key.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__latest_neq
idris.note: The completion position of a match not built on the retracted fact is not the removed position.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__latest_shift
idris.note: The renumbering commutes with the completion position of a surviving key.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__lex_shift
idris.note: The renumbering preserves the pattern-order tiebreak between surviving keys.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__pos_remove
idris.note: A surviving fact's position after a retraction is its renumbered position.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__shift
idris.note: The renumbering a retraction applies to assertion positions: those past the removed position step down by one; the removed position itself is never asked for.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__shift_eq
idris.note: The renumbering preserves equality and inequality of surviving positions.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__shift_lt
idris.note: The renumbering preserves the order of surviving positions.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__shift_max
idris.note: The renumbering commutes with the larger-of on surviving positions.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__sorted_remove
idris.note: A sorted terminal of live activations, none built on the retracted fact, is sorted under the shrunk working memory.

idris.name: Ldet_5_9__ordered
idris.note: THE ORDERED VIEW: the view, and every terminal in agenda order under the engine's working memory.

idris.name: iret_19_2__dispatch_retract_ordered
idris.note: ALPHA DISPATCH ON RETRACT keeps the order, stamped against the working memory it found, over any distinct list of alphas to visit.

idris.name: iret_19_2__dispatch_retract_ordered_step
idris.note: ONE ALPHA VISITED ON RETRACT, admitting the fact, keeps the order under the working memory the retraction found: every chain is right-retracted from a memory that held the fact.

idris.name: iret_19_2__retract_ordered
idris.note: RETRACTING A LIVE FACT keeps the order: the dispatch stamps against the working memory it found; afterwards every activation is live without the fact, so the survivors keep their order under the shrunk working memory. A released match sits at the position its original timetag gives it.

idris.name: iret_7_7__right_retract_ordered
idris.note: RIGHT-RETRACTION KEEPS THE ORDER under the working memory the retraction found: the matches the fact had completed end, and the matches a NOT node releases -- live, not built on the fact -- take the places their keys give them.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__order_after_history
idris.note: THE ORDER THEOREM, closed at the top: after any history from a loaded network -- every input pumped, in order -- every terminal's activations are, in order, the canonical order over working memory of the chain's recompute.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__ordered_recompute
idris.note: UNDER THE ORDERED VIEW every terminal is, in order, the canonical order over working memory of its chain's recompute: the agenda order is a function of the activation set and of working memory, never of how the set was reached. Batched equals incremental in order, and a released match fires where it first completed.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__sorted_unique
idris.note: TWO SORTED TERMINALS WITH THE SAME MATCHES ARE THE SAME LIST: the order is a function of the activation set, never of how the set was reached.

idris.name: iret_7_9__is_blocked_sub
idris.note: Blocking is monotone in working memory: a retraction can release a match, never block one -- why a released match's position is its original one.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__refresh_settled_id
idris.note: Refreshing a settled token leaves it: its blocking is current, and `fired` is cleared only on a release.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__refresh_tok_compose
idris.note: A token settled under a memory, refreshed under a sub-memory and then a sub-memory of that, is the token refreshed under the last.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__refresh_with_compose
idris.note: A token refreshed under a blocking that only ever releases, then refreshed again, is the token refreshed once: a release clears `fired` either way, a token that stays blocked or stays clear keeps it.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__prop_rule_shrink_compose
idris.note: PROPAGATION AFTER SUCCESSIVE RETRACTIONS COMPOSES: a table settled under a memory, propagated over a sub-memory and then over a sub-memory of that, is the table propagated over the last once -- neither propagation adds a match, both keep the same survivors in place, and refreshing along a shrink composes because a retraction only ever releases a `no` pattern. What lets a cascade retract one fact at a time and end where the batch does.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__refresh_fired_released
idris.note: A token released by a refresh is unfired: unblocking mints no history, as on the network side.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__refresh_fired_unblocked
idris.note: An unblocked token keeps its `fired` flag through a refresh.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__prop_agree
idris.note: THE UNBLOCKED TOKENS AFTER A PROPAGATION ARE THE NETWORK'S ACTIVATIONS after the same change: the tuples agree because both sides hold exactly the unblocked matches in the key's order and two sorted lists with the same members are one list; the flags agree because an activation whose match survives is kept on both sides, and a released or new match is unfired on both.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__sorted_tuples_unique
idris.note: TWO SORTED TUPLE LISTS WITH THE SAME MEMBERS ARE ONE LIST: the key is a strict total order on live matches, so the activation set fixes the list. Two engines that agree on the match set agree on the order, as the clause says.

idris.name: iret_8_1__prop_well_shrink
idris.note: PROPAGATION AFTER A FACT LEAVES keeps the table well-formed: nothing is added, and the survivors keep their order under the shrunk memory -- a retraction reorders nothing.

idris.name: iret_8_1__refresh_well
idris.note: Refreshing flags keeps a table well-formed: no tuple moves.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__refresh_tuples
idris.note: Refreshing a token's flags leaves its tuple: blocking and release change no match.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__refresh_live_inv
idris.note: A refreshed token that is fired and unblocked was fired and unblocked: refreshing never sets `fired`, and unblocking clears it.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__refresh_unblocked
idris.note: Refreshing an unblocked token keeps its facts and its `fired`.
